title: Plating and imaging of yeast colonies for segmentation and classification with neural networks
protocol: Mix 1.0 l ddH₂O, 5.0 g Yeast Extract, 30.0 g α-D-Glucose, and 20.0 g Agar until all powder clumps disperse.
Autoclave the mixture at 121°C for 20 min.
Cool down the autoclaved mixture to 50°C under constant stirring.
If desired, add antibiotics and stir for 2 min to ensure a homogeneous mixture.
Pour 20 ml of autoclaved agar media into each 10 cm plate.
After solidification (approximately 20 min at room temperature), transfer plates upside down into plastic bags.
Store the plates in a cold room until use or up to two months.
Measure optical density (OD) of liquid culture.
Dilute samples to 100 cells/ml.
Pipette 1 ml onto a cover slip and recount under a microscope.
Dilute to 500 cells/100 ml (per plate).
Homogeneously distribute 100 ml/plate with glass beads.
Transfer cells from a plate into a 1 ml H2O containing Eppendorf tube using a pipette tip.
Mix well by vortexing.
Dilute 1:100.
Pipette 1 ml onto a cover slip and count cells under the microscope.
Dilute to 500 cells/100 ml (per plate).
Homogeneously distribute 100 ml/plate with glass beads.
Incubate plates upside down at 30°C for 5-7 days.
Place plate on a dark black background.
Adjust camera height or zoom so the entire plate fits into one image.
Run the classification pipeline as described in (Carl et al; bioRxiv, doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/801845).
Download and install the required python packages.
Download the classification pipeline script.
Place all images that you would like to classify into the same folder.
Run the pipeline as described on the github page.
